Your principal developer identifies the following query in a code review and recommends replacing it with a subquery COUNT:

// Original query:
MATCH (u:User)-[r:RATED]->(m:Movie {title: 'Frozen'})
RETURN COUNT(r) as ratingCount

// Recommended query:
MATCH (u:User)-[:RATED]->(m:Movie {title: 'Frozen'})
RETURN COUNT { (u)-[:RATED]->(m) } as ratingCount
What is the main benefit of the recommended query?
options: Relationships aren't expanded in memory since the query uses a static count.
The results will be more accurate as it handles null values better.
The query is easier to read and understand for new developers.
The updated query is shorter and more concise.

questions.question:
Suppose we want to return a list of all movies for each actor whose name contains "Tom". What is wrong with this code?

MATCH (a:Person)
WHERE a.name  CONTAINS "Tom"
WITH a, a.name AS actorName
CALL
{
	MATCH (a)-[:ACTED_IN]->(m:Movie)
	RETURN collect(m.title) as movies
}
RETURN actorName, movies
options: You must pass a as a variable to the subquery.
You can only pass property values to a subquery, not nodes.
You must add WITH movies, actorName after the CALL {} block.
The syntax is invalid. You must use GraphQL.
